#2807. Discussion: Is today’s game a must win for the Panthers?

It's rare that an interconference match-up in November has enough stakes to be considered a must win, but the Carolina Panthers might find themselves in a position where that's the case. They're currently just 4-5, but that's enough to lead the NFC South by a game over the Saints and Buccaneers with the Falcons just one extra loss behind. It's a tightly packed race, and by rule, someone has to win the division and make the playoffs.

The Panthers are coming off a key step towards winning the division with a road win over the Saints last week. Up next is the Ravens. Going into the season, this looked like a tough game, probably even penciled in as a loss for the Panthers. But now the Ravens are on their third string quarterback who they just traded for like two weeks ago. The Panthers are favorites, so they should win this game. But the question is, do they have to?

MY TAKE: Yes it is. The Panthers still could win the division with a loss, but their road will be a whole lot tougher for it. After this game, the Panthers will have seven games left on their schedule. Three of those are against NFC South rivals with one game apiece. The Panthers can win all of those. But winning all of those gets them to seven wins, and seven wins seems very unlikely to make the playoffs in a 17 game schedule, no matter how bad the division is. They have to get at least one or two more wins from outside the division from here on out, and this is by far the best chance for them to do it.

The rest of the Panthers non-division schedule looks like this:

This is definitely the Panthers' chance to get a win, and it's very likely it's the only game they'll be favored in. The Steelers are gettable, but the other three teams on this schedule have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. It's hard to see the Panthers stealing one of those games.

The best path for the Panthers to make the playoffs is to take care of their division games and steal at least one more game outside the division. The rest of the non-divisional schedule is brutal, so that makes today a must win game, in my opinion.

#2804. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the new tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders big and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options."

#2802. Down Tatum, White, and Robinson, Celtics lose to lowly Kings 97-96

The Celtics suffered their most embarrassing loss of the season on Saturday night, losing to the now two-win Sacramento Kings, 97-96.

It was the third quarter that pushed the Kings over the top as Boston shot 5-of-26 from the field (missed all thirteen three-pointers) in the period and were outscored 35-13. It was a great game for Mike Conley, who scored 19 points and was a +17.

The Celtics were missing three key players in this one; Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Mitchell Robinson all sat out this game. They started Payton Pritchard, Sam Hauser, Paul George, Hugo Gonzalez and Neemias Queta. It was the first start of the season for both Hauser and Pritchard. Meanwhile, the Kings started, Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, Keegan Murray, De'Andre Hunter and Domantas Sabonis. Ben Simmons and Maxime Raynaud remained out as neither player has played all season.

It was a really hot start for the Celtics as they scored the first 7 points of the game — buckets from Pritchard, Queta and George, led to a Sacramento timeout.

The C's missed 11 of their first 13 three point attempts as Sacramento went on a 21-5 run to take a 23-19 lead.

Sam Hauser hit a corner three at the buzzer to give the Celtics a 27-25 lead at the end of the first quarter. Hauser led the team in scoring with 6 points while Hugo Gonzalez had 5.

Mike Conley was the first point guard off of the bench instead of Devin Carter in what was his return to Sacramento. Conley chipped in right away with 5 points and 2 steals in his first 4 minutes of action.

He then had a sweet pass to Ron Harper Jr.

The Celtics took a lot of threes in the first half but most of them did not go in. They went 9/33 from beyond the arc in the half. They also fouled too much in the first half; the Kings spent much of the 2nd quarter in the bonus.

The Celtics led 54-41 after the first half. Hauser had 4 of the 9 Celtics threes and 12 points. The defense was awesome holding the Kings to 41 points and being the reason Boston led by 13 at the break.

The Celtics three-point struggles continued into the 3rd quarter as the Kings made a run to cut the Celtics lead to 2 at 60-58. The primary reason for the Kings run was the Celtics defense fell off. The Kings scored 17 points in the first 6:31 of the 3rd quarter. The Celtics called a timeout and turned it over out of the timeout as Sacramento tied the game. The Kings led entering the 4th, 76-67.

There are really no words to describe how the quarter went. They were bad on offense and defense and this is against the worst 3rd quarter team in the NBA entering the night — the Kings 3rd quarter net rating had been -23.7.

The Celtics started the 4th quarter with a new lineup.

They scored the first 1o points of the quarter to take the lead by 1. Mike Conley had 6 of the 10 points.

The two teams were tied at 82 after the Kings regained a 5-point lead but another Conley three and a Luka Garza put back knotted the game up.

Then, on a night the Celtics could not buy a three, Neemias Queta hit a three.

Darius Acuff hit a tough mid-range shot to put the Kings up 1, followed by a Paul George offensive rebound to put the Celtics up 1, then Acuff made 2 free throws to put the Kings up 1 with 40.5 seconds to go.

After Queta and Acuff traded 2 free throws each, Payton Pritchard, who had struggled all night, hit a clutch mid-range shot to put the Celtics up 1 with 11.8 seconds to go as the Kings called timeout.

Keegan Murray got an offensive rebound and put back right over Devin Carter and Hugo Gonzalez to put the Kings up 97-96 with 5 seconds left.

Payton Pritchard missed what would have been a game winning shot and the Celtics lost 97-96 as the Kings got their 2nd win of the season.

In a game Boston lost by 1 points, they missed 10 free throws.

For what it's worth, Darius Acuff Jr. is a star. The way he took over the game late after struggling all night was really impressive.

The C's shot 34% from the field and 22% from three while the Kings shot 41% from the field and 27% from three. The Celtics next game is Sunday in San Francisco against the Warriors at 8:30 pm EST.

#2800. Takeaways from UH's win at West Virginia: Cougars bounce back, Keisean Henderson arrives

MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - Five takeaways from No. 20 Houston's 34-31 victory over West Virginia on Saturday:

How would the Cougars respond after a disappointing performance in a 42-32 loss at Colorado?

The Cougars showed plenty of fight and, while the defense still showed some cracks and the offense sputtered at times, it was a Big 12 road win. UH also remains in position to reach the 10-win mark in consecutive seasons for the first time in program history.

"We had to flush it out and come back stronger," running back Makhi Hughes said. "That's what we did."

All the talk has been about the Keisean Henderson era beginning in 2027. Well, that's still the case, but UH fans got a sneak peek when the true freshman made his first career start in place of injured fifth-year senior Conner Weigman. Henderson had some impressive moments (his 68-yard touchdown pass to Amare Thomas on the third play of the game) but it was what he didn't do that should be praised.

The heralded freshman knew when to throw the ball away. He knew when not to try and do too much. He trusted his pass protection and had enough patience to stay in the pocket long enough to see things develop. He also showed his ability to run, including an 18-yard keeper.

His game management down the stretch resembled that of a veteran, not a first-year quarterback who had been limited to 17 snaps all season. The future is bright for Henderson.

You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter.

UH's offensive line, a Joe Moore Award semifinalist for the best in the nation, gave Keisean Henderson plenty of time to work. Henderson averaged 3.19 seconds to throw on all dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Only one of Henderson's two sacks was credited to the offensive line. "We got a couple of blitzes and got a little pressure on him, but outside of that, it was way too much time to throw the ball," West Virginia coach Rich Rodriguez said. We'll give the line a pass for the three false starts.

That seems to be what the UH defense has seen in the past month. It was another heavy dose of runs Saturday as the Cougars allowed a season-high 329 yards to the Mountaineers. That followed the 249 yards allowed by UH in a double-digit loss at Colorado. In the first seven games this season, UH was among the best in the nation, allowing an average 82.6 yards per game. In the last four games, UH is allowing 241.5 points per game. But as one UH staffer said leaving the field, "We made the stops when it mattered."

On its final five drives, West Virginia missed a field goal and had four punts. After allowing a touchdown on the opening drive of the second half, UH did not allow any points over the final 27 ½ minutes.

Jonathan Dimas has been money all season, connecting on 13 of his 15 field goal attempts, an 86.7% success rate.

Dimas delivered a 23-yard field goal as time expired and had a 34-yarder late in the third quarter. His 54-yard try just before halftime had the distance but hit the left upright. It would have been a school record.

A week earlier, Dimas had a career-high 52-yard field goal at Colorado.

"Tremendous season," coach Willie Fritz said.

#2797. Mike Brown pushing for faster offense from sluggish Knicks

"Last-last," Brown asked, "or second-to-last?"

Entering Saturday, the Knicks sat at the very bottom of the NBA in pace, averaging 94.91 possessions per game. Brown repeatedly has urged his team to play with pace since taking over last year, but it's a rare desire that has not come to fruition.

New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown reacts during the fourth quarter against the Portland Trail Blazers in New York, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Getty Images

The reality is that this is not an overly athletic roster that thrives in transition. This group of veteran players never will be a unit that loves to get up and down the floor. Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby are more methodical scorers who prefer to set up themselves in the frontcourt.

Brown knows that, so while he will continue to preach pace, he values something else that serves as an indication of whether his offense is functioning properly, something that doesn't necessarily require the natural athleticism they lack.

"We have to make sure that every time we cut, it's a scoring cut and our decisions are quick," Brown said before a 97-96 Knicks win, which required a buzzer-beating 3 from Mikal Bridges to escape after blowing a 26-point second-half lead.

When the Knicks offense kicked into gear during their championship run last year, it was evident.

With Towns operating as a hub, the four other Knicks on the floor constantly cut and set off-ball screens around him. The ball moved quickly, swinging side to side constantly. Towns, along with Anunoby and Jordan Clarkson, did not play Saturday.

Landry Shamet, who scored 20 points, shoots a jumper over Toumani Camara during the Knicks' buzzer-beating win over the Trail Blazers on Nov. 21, 2026, at the Garden. Jason Szenes for New York Post

"You can tell when a guy goes from Point A to Point B with a little bit of velocity," Brown said. "A guy like Landry Shamet, he is doing it every single time. With him shooting the ball the way he's shooting it, that gravity that he carries when he moves, you can't really see it or feel it if you don't know the game well. But when he moves that quickly from Point A to Point B, everybody is just leaning just a little bit in that direction, which may create an opening or an advantage for your teammate that's away from him."

It's a reason why Shamet's role keeps growing. Among the five starters, though, it's something they've had to reestablish after a sluggish first few games of the season.

The Knicks aren't quick in transition. Once they're set in the frontcourt, though, they're capable of playing quickly.

It's when they are at their best. It takes pressure off Brunson having to orchestrate everything. It sets up open catch-and-shoot opportunities for Anunoby and Mikal Bridges. It allows Josh Hart to utilize his passing ability and set up teammates.

"Trying to get everybody to do that all the time is huge," Brown said. "Because the defense doesn't have a chance to catch up, they don't have a chance to get set, and they just gotta react. And sometimes they'll overreact because you're going so hard. And you can see it as the game goes along. If guys aren't doing it, we try to mention it to him."

A slow team finding a way to play fast — that's crucial to the Knicks' success.

#2794. The Nasdaq is in freefall. Here's one stock to look at

I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market. Its advice was surprisingly useful: avoid panic selling and look for opportunities. A 40 VIX, which it touched Friday, might provide those opportunities. Specifically, a higher VIX (higher options premiums) signals fear, but it also creates an opportunity to sell elevated premium in some premium stocks, like Amazon.

Amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. AWS revenue rose 39.3% YoY in the third quarter, and management reported a $578 billion backlog. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion. However, infrastructure investment accelerated, resulting in more than $42 billion in negative cash flow. The competing forces of accelerating growth and the cost of supplying it could keep the stock in its range over the next four weeks. Its shares are only off 14% from its recent highs, comparatively better than the Nasdaq Composite's near 19% decline.

AWS demand supports the lower end of the range. The backlog gives Amazon a basis for adding capacity even as investors scrutinize the cash cost. Cash spending could temper an upside rerating.

#2792. Lakers desperately need Austin Reaves. When will LA star return?

The Los Angeles Lakers put together a nine-game winning streak to start the month of November. It just recently came to an end with a 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz at home on Nov. 18.

Shooting guard Austin Reaves contributed to the early success but landed awkwardly on his left heel after missing a transition dunk attempt in the Lakers' eventual 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 11. He's been out of the lineup ever since but has continued to work his way back.

Reaves' injury is among the most concerning for the Lakers. While he's been considered day-to-day by coach JJ Redick, Reaves has missed the last four games.

Redick told reporters on Nov. 20 that he's hoping to have Reaves back in the lineup sooner rather than later.

The earliest Reaves could return would be the Lakers' next game, at home against the Utah Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23.

"I think getting through this stretch for all of our guys is important," Redick said. "We've made a lot of progress. … We're trying to manage (Reaves') pain. So hopefully he'll be back in one of the next two games."

Reaves and the Lakers' medical staff had previously opted against having imaging done on the injury.

Quentin Grimes has taken on more responsibility when the Lakers have been without a star player in the lineup.

"I'm not set in stone on anything," Redick said about fitting Grimes in as a starter when Reaves returns. "The reality is that Quentin has been a starter, either A.R. or Luka has been off, so naturally he will assume some of that usage."

Grimes scored a game-high 47 points on 16-of-24 shooting from the field against the Charlotte Hornets on Nov. 18.

Reaves has started all 12 of the games he's played in for the Lakers this season. The guard is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting 51.3% from the field and 40.9% from beyond the arc.

#2790. Brian Flores vs. Kyle Shanahan is ultimate 'Sunday Night Football' chess match | Opinion

Like you, me and millions of others, Phil Simms can't wait to see how it all goes down in Mexico City on Sunday night, when the NFL's most dominating defense collides with the league's top-ranked offense.

The Minnesota Vikings (7-2) have allowed just six touchdowns all season, yielding an NFL-low average of 14 points per game. The San Francisco 49ers (8-1) have scored more touchdowns (37) than any team in the league while amassing the most yards.

Something's gotta give. And oh, by the way: those big-time units just happen to be directed by two of the sharpest minds in the NFL universe, with Minnesota's D created by coordinator Brian Flores while 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan pushes the buttons for the prolific offense.

Complete with that matchup of wits, it's a subplot for "Sunday Night Football" (8:20 p.m. ET) that the folks at NBC are undoubtedly tinkled pink about.

"Without question, this is the best D-coordinator and the best O-coordinator in the NFL," Simms, the former Giants quarterback and Super Bowl XXI MVP, told USA TODAY Sports from his home in New Jersey. "If you try to argue that I would just go, 'You're stupid.'

"All I know isc in that chair, and I can't wait for this game."

If the names aren't moving enough – the 49ers surround Brock Purdy with Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and Trent Williams, among others, while the Vikings bring Harrison Smith, Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner, among others – let a few more numbers speak.

The Vikings lead the league with 37 sacks and hold opposing QBs to the lowest efficiency rating at 69.5. The 49ers have given up the third-fewest sacks (13) while Purdy ranks second in the NFL with a 115.2 passer rating.

That efficient knack for Purdy will undoubtedly face its toughest test the season because the Vikings blitz at the highest rate in years (maybe ever), bringing extra rushers on more than 80% of the snaps. Purdy, in his fifth NFL season, can vouch for that. He was sacked six times and threw an interception in the last meeting between the teams, a 23-17 Vikings win in 2024. In 2023, Minnesota collected just one sack but intercepted Purdy twice in a 22-17 victory.

Shanahan said this week that experience has facilitated Purdy's growth to the point nothing will surprise him because there is little he hasn't seen. We'll see how that plays out. Flores' knack involves unpredictability that comes with designing blitzes that may not have shown up on video.

"Look, I played 15 years," Simms said. "I think I know every blitz, have seen it or whatever. But that's just not true. I watch the Vikings every week and it never fails. There's something new every week.

"I don't know if you can get ready for it in a week. That's one of their little secrets of power."

Still, as sharp as Flores is, there are other master strategists all across the NFL. Why is Minnesota's architect able to get away with such a blitz-heavy scheme – remember the tried-and-true football axiom, "live by the blitz, die by the blitz" – without getting burned?

While Shanahan mentioned the commitment to Minnesota's aggressiveness as vital to the effectiveness, listen to another Super Bowl MVP quarterback.

"They have so many smart players," Kurt Warner, who led the Rams to a Super Bowl 34 crown as triggerman for the "Greatest Show on Turf," told USA TODAY Sports.

"He does a great job teaching his guys the nuances, those details," Warner added of Flores. "It's, 'If we're going to do this, this is how it has to go.' But it's also having players with a great feel, great instincts. They understand the big picture. 'I've got to rush the C-gap, but I've got to know what the quarterback is doing and what the formation is.' They can add extra layers to it."

That includes the versatility that plays hand in hand with disguising intentions. Maybe no Vikings defender illustrates as much like Van Ginkel, the outside linebacker who has generated his team-high 8 ½ sacks on just 175 rush snaps, while also logging 103 snaps in coverage – more than any edge rusher in the league.

Of course, the 49ers offense has its own brand of versatility. McCaffrey, the NFL's leading scorer (80 points, including 13 TDs), has long been one of the league's most lethal dual threats with receiving skills out of the backfield on par with many wideouts. Deebo Samuel Sr. is the powerful receiver who frequently lines up in the backfield. Kyle Juszczyk is not your classic fullback, aligning all across the formation as another type of Swiss Army knife.

In some regards, including versatility, the Vikings defense and 49ers offense provide mirror images.

Which gets us back to Shanahan, long one of the league's best play-callers. As much as he marvels at play designs that create wide-open windows for passing targets, Simms notes the resourcefulness.

The 49ers have produced their big numbers this season – and tied for the most victories in the NFL – despite having the wide receiver corps decimated by injuries. Last year, Shanahan took the 49ers to the playoffs despite losing Purdy for several games on top of setbacks to Kittle and McCaffrey (in addition to the season-ending injuries to defensive stars Fred Warner and Nick Bosa).

"Kyle, he's going to do whatever it takes," Simms said.

He thought about the flow that Mac Jones had last season while filling in for Purdy and asked: "Look at Kyle Shanahan's career and tell me which quarterback has ever played bad under him?"

The lineup would include Kirk Cousins, back in Minnesota to revive the Vikings' playoff hopes. Matched against San Francisco's defense on Sunday night, he represents another layer of a subplot. Shanahan was Cousins' first NFL offensive coordinator when the quarterback broke into the NFL with Washington in 2012.

Here's to a great chess match. One thing for certain: There is no shortage of respect between Shanahan and Flores.

"Where do I start?" said Flores, using the same word – elite – to describe the 49ers' rushing attack, pass protection and play design. "All of it is elite."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Brian Flores vs. Kyle Shanahan is ultimate 'Sunday Night Football' chess match | Opinion

#2789. Wembanyama scores 50 as Spurs crush Pelicans to close homestand

The San Antonio Spurs closed out their three-game homestand with a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans at the Frost Bank Center on Saturday night in front of a sold out crowd, which included one very special celebrity guest, singer and actress Selena Gomez.

Victor Wembanyama posted 50 points, 18 rebounds, 5 three-pointers, and 5 blocks in 32 minutes. At one point during the first half, Wembanyama hit one of his five threes on the night, turned towards the crowd and smiled in Gomez's direction.

"I had to show off for Selena (Gomez)," he said, smiling as he answered.

Wembanyama came out aggressive from the opening tip, scoring 17 of the Spurs' 32 points in the opening quarter. He went to rim for dunks, hit free throws, and scored from the mid range. San Antonio had 30 assists on the night and 14 of those were off a made Wemby basket. Nothing New Orleans did worked on this night to stop the Spurs' French star from accomplishing his goal of scoring 50 points, no matter how hard they tried.

Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley doubled Wembanyama with multiple players, but the Spurs' forward backed down the smaller player right into the paint or when he was triple teamed, he found Julian Champagnie or Devin Vassell for an open three.

"I thought he started the game off aggressive," Spurs Head Coach Mitch Johnson said of Wembanyama after the game. "It's so interesting when people play like that, especially with his talent and then it helps with your shots. I thought he did a really good job of playing with force."

Despite Wembanyama's great night, Johnson still had a criticism for his star player and that is his passing. Late in the half, Wemby secured a defensive rebound and brought the ball up court. Instead of finding the open Keldon Johnson, the French star pulled up for three and missed, ignoring his open teammate.

"Keldon has to have the ball in that moment," Mitch Johnson said. "When you play the right way, things like that happen."

As good as the Spurs looked on Saturday, they still struggled in the non-Wemby minutes. New Orleans outscored the Spurs 22-13 in the first half when Wembanyama sat, but things were even when he sat in the second half. The reason? Johnson put in Luke Kornet, Harrison Barnes, and Carter Bryant. However, he kept Devin Vassell and Stephon Castle on the floor with that second unit.

"I thought we had some moments where we did a really good job defensively in terms of shrinking the floor and showing crowds and gang rebounding," Mitch Johnson said. "That group, probably, the worst minutes of the non Victor, has nothing to do with Luke, in my opinion. It's when we take quick shots, and then we're in transition defense a lot, and we're on our heels."

As a result of those lineup changes, Castle turned it on and scored 19 points on the night to go along with six assists.

"It's been reflective ever since he's been on this team," Wembanayama said of Castle. "He's been impactful in a meaningful way and he's impacted winning ever since he arrived here."

Keldon Johnson had 10 points off the bench, scoring in double figures for the fourth time in the last five games. If he can continue to deliver at that level consistently, the bench unit will be much improved as the season goes on. "When I do the right things on the court, the scoring will come," Keldon said after the game.

De'Aaron Fox slipped on a wet spot on the floor during the first half and was limping a bit before being taken out of the game. He would return later and Mitch Johnson said after the game that Fox was fine. Still, Fox scored just 5 points on 1-for-4 shooting and one has to wonder if his hip injury is bothering him.

The Spurs are now 14-3 on the season and will return to the court on Monday night when they face the Sacramento Kings at 9 p.m.

#2788. ESPN’s ‘College GameDay’ returning to Wake Forest for first time since 2020

Last Saturday, the No. 11 Wake Forest Demon Deacons put the country on notice with a 49-7 win over SMU.

That morning, Kirk Herbstreit and Pat McAfee had picked SMU on ESPN's College GameDay, and after that pick aged spectacularly poorly, they recorded a video in shame.

Herbstreit and McAfee will now have a chance to apologize to Wake Forest in person.

On Saturday night, College GameDay announced that it will travel to Winston-Salem, North Carolina, for Wake Forest's regular-season finale against Duke next Saturday, Nov. 28.

This will mark just the second instance College GameDay has visited Winston-Salem, with the first trip coming in September 2020.

It will be an abject failure unless GameDay brings out the couple who argued (and made up!) during Jesse Palmer and Joe Tessitore's call of Wake Forest's win over Georgia Tech. America desperately needs the backstory.

The Demon Deacons improved to 10-1 with a 50-29 victory over Georgia Tech on Saturday, and with that, they punched a ticket to the ACC Championship Game for the first time since 2021. There, Wake Forest will face the No. 7 Miami Hurricanes, who outlasted Virginia Tech to improve to 10-1 late Saturday night.

Wake Forest will be seeking revenge come Dec. 5, as its only loss came against Miami in Week 3. But first, the Demon Deacons and Duke (7-4) will face off at Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, and kickoff time is yet to be announced.

#2787. Top Wall Street analysts favor these 3 dividend stocks for strong returns

Investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a company's financials.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company announced a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

After hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta said that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

Devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta said. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

Mehta, a 5-star analyst, said Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the company to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

"Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta said.

Mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

Energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The company recently announced third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The company delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and announced the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman said. The project is supported by 20-year firm transportation agreements and is expected to enter service in 2030. ET expects to ultimately own 51% of the $1.6 billion project.

The 5-star analyst said that Energy Transfer lowered its 2026 capital spending outlook to $5.5 billion (midpoint of the guidance range) from $5.75 billion due to project timing. Energy Transfer expects capex to rise to $7 billion in 2027, while Gabelman projects $5 billion in both 2028 and 2029, based on disclosed projects.

Gabelman also highlighted management's commentary about optimization initiatives contributing an incremental $800 million to 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a larger benefit than in recent years. "A return to less commodity volatility should the [Middle East] war end could bring some relative downside, though this is offset by continued strong growth prospects," he said.

Gabelman ranks No. 397 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.4%. See Energy Transfer KPIs on TipRanks.

Oil and gas exploration and production company ConocoPhillips (COP) delivered better-than-expected Q3 performance. The company announced an 11% hike in its quarterly dividend to 93 cents per share, effective with the Q4 dividend payable on December 1. Based on the dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, COP yields about 2.6%.

Following the Q3 results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin repeated a buy rating on ConocoPhillips, citing strong potential for further dividend increases. Margolin also trimmed his price target to $185 from $189 to reflect timing effects and the WAHA forward curve, though he said that COP could still re-rate as its natural portfolio lifecycle provides stronger protection against inflationary pressures than peers. The Waha forward curve tracks future natural gas prices based on the West Texas Waha hub.

Margolin, another 5-star analyst, highlighted that ConocoPhillips' Q3 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $3.27 was well above Wells Fargo and the Street's estimates of $3.04 and $3.05, respectively. Earnings were driven by solid price realizations, partially offset by higher depletion, depreciation and amortization and purchased commodities.

Margolin also noted COP's dividend increase and said the accelerated buyback enabled by current commodity prices could further support long-term dividend growth. He sees the possibility of ConocoPhillips' dividend growth rate exceeding its current 6% cost of equity into the end of the decade. Margolin expects COP to sustain an 8% dividend compound annual growth rate through 2029 while repurchasing $6.4 billion of stock annually, and reducing net debt-to-capital to less than 9% by the end of 2028 based on the assumption of an average Brent crude oil price of $75 a barrel.

"The message on the 3Q call was similar to that of 2Q, reiterating the moderation in reinvestment rate and commitment to dividend growth through the Willow start-up and after," Margolin said.

#2783. Eagles News: ESPN predicts a Philadelphia upset

Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Might the Philadelphia Eagles actually win a football game today?! I'm not counting on it. But I do think it's more possible after seeing the Pittsburgh Steelers drop from being 4.5-point road favorites to 3.5-point road favorites.

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

NFL Week 11 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more – ESPN

Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday. Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard Mason McCormick (ankle). Eagles backup QB Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver DeVonta Smith potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.

Should the Eagles want Shane Steichen back? – BGN

The Eagles have been so bad this season that they've forced me to change what I write about. I really enjoy studying opposing teams for the weekly previews, but I'm already more interested in what the Eagles might look like next year. So, over the remaining weeks of the season, I'm going to examine potential coaching candidates and some offenses and defenses that interest me. Obviously, this depends on the Eagles making changes, and in this particular case, the Colts letting Shane Steichen go. Neither is guaranteed. However, I thought it would be interesting to look beyond the record and examine whether Steichen is still someone Eagles fans should want back.

Steelers activate WR Roman Wilson ahead of Eagles matchup – Behind The Steel Curtain

The Steelers are getting one of their top wide receivers back ahead of Week 11's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Pittsburgh announced Saturday that wide receiver Roman Wilson has been activated to the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's game. In addition, the team announced the signing of edge rusher K.J. Henry from the practice squad to the roster. The two signings fill the open spots on the Steelers' roster. The Henry signing follows the Steelers announcing outside linebacker Nick Herbig as out for Sunday's game. Now, Pittsburgh has an open slot on its practice squad.

Eagles locker room notebook: Taking stock of Makai Lemon ahead of full-circle matchup vs. Pittsburgh Steelers – PHLY Eagles

Expect to see Ty Robinson take some of the nose-tackle snaps previously reserved for Jordan Davis at the heart of the Eagles defense this season. He's an unconventional fit for the position at 6-foot-5, 288 pounds, but Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said the second-year lineman out of Nebraska has gotten extensive work in practice playing as a zero technique and believes he can hold up even with a relatively smaller frame for the role. "The nose tackle isn't totally the position that is viewed as it was in the past," Fangio said. "When there was a two back running game and there was a lot of [isolation runs] where he would get a lot, a lot of double teams. It still happens, but not as much as it used to." Robinson said it would be "big shoes" to fill in for Davis, but wasn't concerned about his size in the new role. "All last year I was learning all three positions," Robinson said. "The playbook is the easiest part now. It's just about going out there and executing and trying to fill the shoes of Jordan Davis. And those are some big shoes to fill. … It's just about the heart of the dog in the fight. I go against Jordan Mailata every day. That dude's massive. We go against massive dudes. It's nothing discouraging, just going out there and playing the way I know how to play."

Eagles notebook: Nolan Smith reacts to the Jordan Davis trade – NBCSP

Nolan Smith and Jordan Davis were teammates at Georgia and then became teammates again in the NFL. They have been friends for a long time. But there's no time to be sad. "Man, he's a great guy," Smith said on Friday. "That's part of the business. That's how it goes. I'm pretty sure Jacksonville is picking up a good player. But we have to focus on us. We have leaders in this locker room. We've got guys who can lead and push guys." Davis was traded to the Jaguars ahead of the trade deadline last week and this was the first chance to catch up with Smith since the trade. So it has been over a week since it all went down. Jalen Carter, who also played with Davis at Georgia before becoming teammates in the NFL, was again not available to reporters this week. The return on the Davis trade for the Eagles was undeniable. Getting a first-round pick and second-round pick for Davis represented incredible value. But it doesn't mean they won't miss Davis. "Man, it was special," Smith said of their time together in Philly. "But that time come and go, man. I'm still playing with guys that I played with at Georgia. But that was a real special moment, though."

Game Preview vs. Steelers: Six storylines to follow Sunday – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

Handling the Steelers' blitz game. There are individual stars here – T.J. Watt has 7.5 sacks and 9 tackles for loss – but it's the collective that makes the Steelers so good on defense. They bring pressure and they aren't afraid to expose their back end to one-on-one matchups and that's why having Smith is so critical. They can win those matchups. But the Eagles first have to handle pressure. Quarterback Joe Milton III said he has confidence in how much he worked to advance his understanding of the scheme and of what Pittsburgh does, so we will see how the Eagles react. Milton ran for 65 yards against the Giants two weeks ago. He can gash the blitz with his legs, but the Eagles also need to make the passing game go and avoid negative plays.

Oren Burks placed on IR by Bengals – Cincy Jungle

The Cincinnati Bengals have placed [Eagles Super Bowl LIX champion] linebacker Oren Burks on the injured reserve list with a groin injury, the team announced on Saturday. Burks, a ninth-year player, has played in all nine games this season, totaling seven tackles and one tackle for loss on defense to go with nine tackles on special teams. He suffered his injury during the team's Week 10 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

NY Giants' pass defense has been much better than expected – Big Blue View

Fast-forward nine games, and the Giants' secondary has been much, much, better than anticipated under [former Eagles assistant] Dennard Wilson, Donald D'Alesio, and Addison Lynch. The Giants are currently fielding the NFL's fourth-best defense in total yardage allowed (2,751 total yards). They're third-best in passing yardage allowed per game (184.1 yards per game), second in yards per completion allowed (9.8 yards per completion), and 2nd in yards per attempt allowed (6.2 yards per attempt). The Giants are accomplishing this feat with smothering coverage from their starting corners. Both Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II have been incredibly sticky in man coverage, allowing little separation for receivers.

Cowboys passing attack should shine, pass rush could struggle – Blogging The Boys

The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday's matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league's worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the air, especially with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens coming off productive performances. There are still reasons to be cautious. The Cowboys' defense has been a disaster this year, and Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward has improved over the past few weeks. With Dallas also changing its defensive play-calling, this matchup could tell us a lot about the team's direction. Here are two players to buy and one area to sell ahead of Sunday's game.

Why Daronte Jones has Washington Commanders defense trending up – Hogs Haven

Washington's defense will be tested by the Cincinnati Bengals offense, which has scored 30-plus points in their last five games. Quarterback Joe Burrow might be this defense's kryptonite, considering how well he and the Bengals coaching staff handles the blitz. Burrow has the third-highest success rate when facing five rushers or more and has the NFL's highest completion rate at 73.4% against the blitz. Also, Jones said that Cincinnati prioritizes protection and does a good job disguising their work in pass pro. Does all that impact how Jones will call Monday night's game? He isn't volunteering that. He did provide the primary objective, to keep Burrow off balance. "We have to, in some way shape or form, provide mental stress," Jones said. "He can't be sitting back there knowing our coverage. We have to find a way to change the picture. It's going to become a chess match."

This Deshaun Watson reference in GTA 6 is wild – SB Nation

Grand Theft Auto VI is the highest-budget entertainment product in history, and if you've spent any time with the game, you'd understand why. The attention to detail is alarming; the depth of Rockstar's version of Florida is staggering — and the in-game radio has some of the most stunning celebrity DJs imaginable. One of these is comedian Stavros Halkias, who hosts a sports talk radio show that is completely off the rails. Stavros rants about bad performances by Vice City's football teams, claims that every other sport isn't manly — and even has an extended take on why Deshaun Watson did nothing wrong. Watson is never mentioned by name, but listen to this for just a few seconds and it's OBVIOUS.

#2782. 3 biggest positions of need for Patriots to address in future

With the state of the New England Patriots' season in question following Drake Maye's injury, a way-too-early look ahead to the upcoming offseason in 2027 shines a light on three positions that stand out as priorities.

It shouldn't come as a surprise that two of those positions are on the defensive side of the ball. The Patriots entered the season with what was expected to be one of the best defensive units in the NFL. However, recent run-ins with more talented offenses has led to some second-guessing.

The Patriots aren't out of playoff contention, but they are also in a place where they'll be eyeing individual performances even more closely to see who stays and who goes in the offseason. This last stretch of football will be make or break for some players on the roster.

Here are the three biggest positions of need for the team in the offseason:

The Patriots have not gotten strong production from Dre'Mont Jones so far this season, as he has recorded only 1.5 sacks. Elijah Ponder needs to finish the year strong and prove that he is capable of being a reliable pass-rusher over the course of a full 17-game season, though what he has shown through 10 weeks of the year so far has been impressive.

Not only so, but Harold Landry has yet to return from the reserve/physically unable to perform list and is advancing in age, further necessitating a high-end edge rusher to join the team's ranks. Regardless of Ponder's development, New England needs another established presence off the edge.

Adding a high-end pass-rusher in free agency, such as Tuli Tuipulotu, or a championship-caliber performer in Uchenna Nwosu, is a move that the team could benefit from making.

Milton Williams and Christian Barmore give the Patriots a talented starting combination, but the team needs more depth behind the two. Williams has recorded two sacks and five tackles for loss this season, while Barmore has 4.5 sacks, nine tackles for loss and a forced fumble on the year.

Adding a high-quality interior defender such as free agent Kobie Turner might be a smart move for the team to make. New England also needs a high-end third option such as free agent Roy Robertson-Harris, who is capable of potentially stepping into a starting role if the organization decides to trade Barmore in the offseason.

The Patriots have room to add another high-end receiver to complement their existing group. Finding a legitimate third option will give the offense another dynamic weapon and help take pressure off of Drake Maye. If New England's season continues to unravel with Maye sidelined by an ankle injury, the team will stand to gain from having a higher draft selection to use on an elite wide receiver prospect, the likes of Charlie Becker or Nick Marsh.

The open market will also present the Patriots with an opportunity to acquire an established veteran who is capable of contributing immediately next to A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, the likes of Parker Washington and Rashee Rice in free agency.

#2781. CeeDee Lamb fined $23,882 for block the league used as a highlight

When Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb made a downfield block on a George Pickens touchdown catch Sunday against the 49ers, the league’s website was so impressed that the highlight video on NFL.com emphasized Lamb’s block over Pickens’ touchdown.

“Can’t-Miss Play: CeeDee Lamb’s HUGE block springs Pickens free for 39-yard TD,” the caption on the highlight video says.

Calling the play on Fox, Tom Brady praised Lamb, immediately recognizing it as a great downfield block.

But the league’s disciplinary process didn’t think it was so great. Lamb has been fined $23,882 for what the NFL deemed “Unnecessary Roughness: Use of the helmet.”

Lamb confirmed to reporters on Thursday that he had been informed he was getting fined, but he insisted he didn’t make contact with his helmet and found it frustrating that receivers take hits routinely but get fined when they make one.

“I can block, and I’m real good at doing things like that, but I get fined,” Lamb said. “I never touched him with my helmet. . . . I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can’t deliver the punishment.”

Lamb will surely appeal the fine for what looked, both to the league’s website and the league’s all-time greatest player, like a good block.

#2775. Aidan Hutchinson wasn't fined for sack that injured Drake Maye

As expected, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson wasn’t fined for the tackle that may have ended Patriots quarterback Drake Maye’s season.

The weekly announcement from the league includes no fines against Hutchinson.

A question emerged as to whether Hutchinson’s sack of Maye amounted to a hip-drop tackle. During the broadcast, Fox rules analyst (and former NFL senior V.P. of officiating) Mike Pereira said it wasn’t a hip-drop tackle. On Monday, NFL in-house rules analyst Walt Anderson confirmed that it wasn’t a hip-drop tackle.

But it’s not Anderson who makes the decisions on fines. Jon Runyan makes those decisions. Not surprisingly, Runyan decided that the tackle was not a violation of the rules.

Under the rules, a hip-drop tackle happens when a player “grabs the runner with one or both hands or wraps the runner with both arms; and . . . unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips and/or lower body, landing on and/or trapping the runner’s leg(s) at orbelow the knee.” Anderson said Hutchinson did not “unweight” himself or “swivel.”

Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his knee while celebrating the sack. Although it’s not clear whether Maye will play again in 2026, Hutchinson is done for the year.

#2772. NFC North continues its historic dominance

The NFC North continues to perform like no other division in the league.

Three of the teams (Lions, Bears, Vikings) have a record of 7-2 through 10 weeks. The Packers are 6-4.

The combined record of 27-10 equates to a success rate of 73 percent — the highest by any division through Week 10 in NFL history.

Outside the division, the teams of the NFC North are 21-4. The 84-percent success rate is the most for any division through Week 10 since the AFL-NFL merger.

This weekend, the Lions host the Bucs, the Bears host the Saints, and the Vikings face the 49ers in Mexico City.

In theory, all four teams could make the playoffs. That would require the fourth-place team landing higher in the standings than the second-place team in each of the other three divisions.

And that makes Wednesday night’s game between the 6-4 Packers and 6-4 Rams critical to the outcome of the chase for the wild-card berths in the NFC.

#2770. Gameday column: Bills and the current state of strength of schedule

It's like each week there's arisen a new narrative about this Buffalo Bills team.

Leading into Week 11 against the Dolphins, it was all about strength of schedule… probably because of Buffalo's competition — or lack thereof — since the bye week.

I'll be the first to mention that teams are not always what their record says they are.

But what these Bills are doing is subtly different from previous Bills teams during the Josh Allen era.

What has remained the same is Buffalo's regular-season dominance.

Since 2020, the Bills have been the NFL's best team in the regular season. They have the most wins and the highest point differential by an insane margin.

But like I wrote a week ago, the Sean McDermott clubs always had an uncharacteristic stumble or two during said regular season that kept them away out of the No. 1 seat in the AFC playoffs.

Of course today, against the Dolphins, represents one of those "stumble" possibilities with the colossal clash on Thanksgiving against the Chiefs looming. But that's the not the crux of this column.

Are the Bills the best 8-1 team in NFL history? No. Are they the best 8-1 team in the past decade. No.

But they've done exactly what a team should do against the competition level it has faced.

Regarding the aforementioned point differential, it's my absolute favorite measure of team quality… because it's straightforward and pretty darn predictive.

How's this for point differential's stickiness — 11 of the past 12 Super Bowl winners finished the regular season in the Top 6 in point differential. Insane, right? From 2004 – 2025, 17 of 22 of the clubs that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at season's end were a Top 6 point-differential team during the regular season.

And this Bills team enters this AFC East game against the Dolphins second in point differential, at +88.

If Buffalo had been squeaking by lesser opponents regularly, I'd be the first to write their 8-1 feels phony.

And teams can only play the opponents on their schedule.

Among the nine teams at 7-2 or better right now, only the Broncos (.583) and Vikings (.518) have faced a cumulative opponent win percentage above .500. The Bills are third on that list at .480, as their opponents have a combined record of 40-47. The combined record of Chiefs' opponents to date is 34-53 (.391). They're currently in last in that metric.

(another shoutout to Jeremy White from WGR550 who noticed this earlier this week.)

Oh, and as for the strength-of-schedule element that legitimately matters come playoff-seeding time — the Bills currently have the second-best strength of victory at .455, behind only the Broncos, the sole AFC club with a strength of victory over .500.

On this note, the first half of the 2026 NFL season has shown a more sizable gap between the great teams and the noticeably bad ones.

Ahead of Week 11, nine teams with seven or more wins is the most in any season in the NFL since at least 2001. Eight clubs with seven or more losses is tied for the second-most in that time frame.

And, heck, the Bills are 16.5-point favorites at home in the division. The Chiefs are 15.5-point favorites at home against the Cardinals. The Broncos are 10.5-point favorites against the Raiders at home. And the Jaguars are 6-point favorites on the road against the 5-3-1 Giants. Vegas thinks the dichotomy will continue.

The Bills can't focus on proving themselves today against the Dolphins. And they don't have to be concerned about that. They need to stack another win to get to 9-1 before their lengthy test of the holiday season that fittingly begins on Thanksgiving and ends on Christmas, a five-game stretch against the Chiefs, Patriots, Packers, Bears, and Broncos.

We'll know who this Bills team is by then.

But entering that stretch with the AFC's best record possible needs to be the emphasis of today's goal. The quality of opponent is irrelevant.

#2768. Karl-Anthony Towns draws praise from another former coach

Karl-Anthony Towns keeps drawing praise from his former coaches.

Yet another one pointed out how Towns — by playing a central role in the Knicks' championship — disproved much of the criticism that surrounded him throughout his career.

"When we first got him in Minnesota, the playoffs, they were saying how he's a very good player that couldn't win, couldn't get the team to the playoffs," Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori, who served as an assistant with the Timberwolves when Towns was there, said before the Knicks' 97-96 buzzer-beating win Saturday night at Madison Square Garden. "Then, when we got to the playoffs, any time we struggled, it was him that took the fall, unfairly. And I think it was great to see not only the impact that he had on this championship team, but to see the way that he's playing now. … I love KAT; I was happy for him to get to the mountaintop; I was happy for him to play a major role.

"Then, when we made a deep run, they said you can't win a title with him, and he got the blame."

Earlier this week, Timberwolves coach Chris Finch shared while the Knicks were in Minnesota a similar sentiment about Towns, who missed Saturday's game due to an illness, shedding a narrative that he isn't a winner.

Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) did not play in the Knicks' 97-96 buzzer-beating win over the Trail Blazers on Nov. 21, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. NBAE via Getty Images

"Particularly when he started his playoff journey, how much flak he had gotten," Finch said.

"It was fun to see him at the heart of it too, especially as they were kind of tweaking their offense going along and all of his skills came to the surface through that."

Jordan Clarkson, who missed Saturday's game due to right plantar fasciitis, was wearing a boot on his right foot while sitting on the Knicks bench.

OG Anunoby was out Saturday due to left calf soreness.

Towns' absence meant a significant role for James Wiseman, who logged 24 minutes off the bench and recorded five points, six rebounds and three blocks.

"I thought James was great," head coach Mike Brown said. "He ran the floor in both directions, he talked defensively, he impacted the ball at the rim in a phenomenal way. I thought he was really good in his minutes."

He went scoreless Saturday and missed all seven shots he took, including four 3s.

#2766. Knee surgery complicates Puka Nacua's future

On Friday, Rams coach Sean McVay said receiver Puka Nacua will miss “a couple months.” Nacua is reportedly expected to miss a couple months more than that.

Via ESPN, the recovery time following surgery to repair the MCL tear is four to five months. If accurate, that ends Nacua’s 2026 season.

The problem becomes 2027. Nacua is in the last year of his rookie contract. He hasn’t gotten a second deal, due in large part to the off-field issues that recently resulted in a three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy and that culminated in an offseason stay at an in-patient holistic rehab facility after he was “drowning myself” in alcohol.

Based on the ESPN report, Nacua won’t be back to 100 percent before free agency starts. The Rams will have to decide whether to sign him to a new deal, to apply the franchise tag (or the transition tag), or to let him become a free agent.

The injury makes it very difficult for Nacua to land in the Jaxon Smith-Njigba ballpark ($42.15 million per year), even though Nacua’s skills and abilities justify that type of deal.

The situation becomes a prime example of the extent to which off-field issues can complicate a player’s financial interests. Without the New Year’s Eve incident that resulted in a lawsuit and, eventually, a diversion program and, inevitably, a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua would have had his second contract by now. Or, at a minimum, he would have had greater standing to hold out (or hold in) until he got paid what he deserves.

Instead, Nacua continued to carry the injury risk into the final year of his rookie contract. And the injury risk became reality 13 days ago, when McVay dialed up a running play to Nacua on third and 11 while trying to run out the clock in a 20-13 game against the Commanders.

It’s a win for the Rams, who may be able to keep Nacua for a lot less than it would cost to give him a market-level contract. However the Rams play the situation, Nacua’s knee injury will make it easier, and cheaper, to re-sign him.

Ultimately, Nacua may have to prove in 2027 that he is back to full strength. And he may have to get through a full season unscathed to unlock the long-term deal his performances earned — but his off-field complications squandered.

Given the way he plays, it’s hardly a given that Nacua will emerge from the 2027 season with the kind of performance, and health, that will finally get him the contract he should have gotten by now.

#2763. Barlow looks set for season debut with Sixers after long days, ‘miserable' weeks

Barlow looks set for season debut with Sixers after long days, 'miserable' weeks originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Dominick Barlow is on the verge of his season debut with the Sixers.

The team listed Barlow as probable for its Saturday afternoon matchup with the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Barlow practiced Friday and has been making clear progress in his recent on-court work recovering from an injury formally classified as a "lower back stress reaction."

He was a reliable rotation fixture last season, playing 71 regular-season games and starting 59. Barlow posted 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals per contest in 23.8 minutes per game. The Sixers then made a common-sense call to exercise his $3.4 million option for the 2026-27 season.

The 23-year-old described his back injury as "an overuse thing."

"I guess there was an area or maybe I started my (offseason) workouts too early," he said. "I don't know what it was fully in terms of what caused it. Once it happened, it happened. Nothing I can do about it besides try to correct it and get my body feeling as good as possible."

He called the past few weeks "miserable" as he rehabbed and waited on the green light by the Sixers' training staff.

"The days just felt longer," Barlow said. "Trying to be engaged mentally, which I think I've done a good job with, but the physical aspect wasn't there. I'm somebody that's prided himself on competing, being available. Not being able to do that was hard, but I'm excited to kind of put this past me."

With LeBron James and Jaylen Brown on the team now, Barlow won't start at forward when the Sixers are at full strength.

He's still a multi-dimensional frontcourt piece for Sixers head coach Nick Nurse who may very well get substantial opportunities at backup center.

"Just cutting, playing hard, being ready to make the open shot," Barlow said. "And then I don't think you can ever have too much defensive versatility. I think that's something I can bring, try to help us be more versatile."

When Barlow checks into his first game of the season, he'll appreciate the moment.

"You don't really realize what you have until it's not there (anymore)," he said. "I'm just excited to play. …. Just playing the first stint … that's going to be the main thing I'm looking forward to."

Dean Wade (left hamstring soreness/tightness)

#2755. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2747. ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround

'It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers created their two cleanest late-game looks several hours before they needed them.

During Wednesday morning's shootaround in Orlando, Nick Nurse had the Sixers work on offensive material they had not consistently used this season. They tested one of those actions during the first half, returned to it throughout the closing minutes and watched it produce the shots they needed to complete a 17-point comeback.

"We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn't used before, and they ran all that stuff very, very well and very calmly and with composure," Nurse told reporters.

The Sixers have earned six of their 13 wins after trailing by double digits. They are also 11-0 in games that reached clutch time.

Relying on comebacks is not a sustainable plan. The repeated late-game situations, however, have forced a new roster to respond to different lineups, coverages and responsibilities while the season is still young.

Each close finish gives Nurse more information about which players and actions hold up when possessions tighten. Wednesday gave him a new option.

Anfernee Simons' clinching three in the Sixers' 121-116 win over the Magic was the final result of that preparation.

"That last play, we ran that play in the first half," Simons said. "We worked it a couple of times, and in the second half we ran that play every single time down the stretch, and it worked every time.

"It was a play we ran through. [It's gratifying] especially when it's working consistently and you're getting different shots out of it and the opposing team just don't know what to do.

"We just continue to run the play and get the open shots we need."

NBC Sports Philadelphia video producer and Sixers Talk podcast co-host Kevin Rice broke down how the Sixers used its different options to keep Orlando guessing.

The action begins with two players stationed near the elbows. A player on the opposite elbow then sets a screen for the player up top, who receives the ball while moving around it.

The Sixers ran the set three consecutive times during the first half. None of the possessions reached the primary option. Each still produced a quality opportunity.

On the first, Joel Embiid cleared LeBron James out of the area and directed Simons around him for a dribble handoff. Simons received an open three-point look.

Orlando took away the handoff the next time down but left Embiid one-on-one against Wendell Carter Jr. Embiid created enough room to retrieve his own miss and convert an and-one opportunity.

The third attempt pulled Orlando's defense into the paint. Two passes moved the ball through the collapsing coverage and created an open three for VJ Edgecombe.

"We had a little thing where he comes flying off behind Joel, and he doesn't get to do that that much, right?" Nurse said of Simons. "So tonight he gets the opportunity to do it, and it was very good for us on a number of plays."

The Sixers changed the action late without abandoning its initial Horns alignment. Simons moved through the lane to help form a Spain pick-and-roll involving James and Embiid.

On the first late possession, Simons remained near the play after James gained a matchup against Carter. Orlando struggled to sort out its assignments, leaving James open for a 19-foot jumper with 54.8 seconds remaining.

After Jalen Suggs made one of two free throws, the Sixers returned to the same setup. This time, Simons relocated to the left corner after James drew Carter on a switch.

James drove into the paint. Suggs lost track of Simons while responding to the penetration, and James sent the ball toward the corner.

Simons buried the open three to give the Sixers a 119-113 lead with 15 seconds left.

"Bron just penetrated the paint," Simons said. "It kind of got some confusion, and when I was on the dunker and kind of spaced out to the corner, I ended up finding myself wide open for the three, and Bron found me."

The Sixers entered the night without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, their two leading scorers. Simons made his first start with Philadelphia and recorded 18 points in the city where he grew up.

His final basket also illustrated why Nurse believes the Sixers have more to uncover with him.

"When he's out there, they gotta be really careful," Nurse said. "So I think there's some drives he creates, and just about every time he lets it go, whether he's on balance or not, you think it's going in, and that is a big deal. Like, that is a big deal.

"And again, I think we're still a ways away from really unlocking him to being even more part of some of the things we can do with him to create more shots."

Philadelphia is now 11-0 in clutch games. The finish in Orlando provided a more specific explanation than experience or shot-making alone.

The Sixers installed a set in the morning, explored its counters and trusted it when the game tightened. James supplied the patience to read Orlando's coverage. Embiid occupied the middle of the action. Simons moved without the ball, and Edgecombe remained ready to shoot.

James said his heart rate drops when close games increase the pressure on everyone else.

"I mean, experience," James said. "A guy that's seen every situation this league has to offer. It's nothing I haven't seen. And, you know, in the moments where people's heart rate goes up or anxiety goes up, mine is pretty low. It's actually lower, you know."

The Sixers still have more actions and reads to learn as Nurse becomes familiar with his new personnel, but their latest win showed their innate ability to adapt in big moments.

"I think we're still a long ways away from knowing all the reads and all that stuff because it's just a little early, right?" Nurse said.

#2744. Josh Allen is one score away from four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns

Bills quarterback Josh Allen has become something that few quarterbacks are — a rushing-touchdown machine.

In nine 2026 games, Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns. With only one more, he’ll have his fourth straight season with 12 or more rushing touchdowns.

Via NBC Sports research, that would make him only the fifth player in NFL history to have four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns.

The others were all running backs. LaDainian Tomlinson did it six times. Shaun Alexander accomplished it five times. Derrick Henry and Adrian Peterson did it four times each.

Henry, who has 10 this year, is two short of running his own streak to five seasons in a row.

Allen’s next rushing touchdown will give him 91 for his career, putting him in a tie for 12th all time with Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis. Given that Allen is only in his ninth season, the all-time rushing-touchdown record of 164, held my Emmitt Smith, could eventually be in jeopardy.
