#2743. Five sports clubs at Florida State you should know about

Every week, Florida State club sports athletes are sailing on the lakefront, climbing at a local rock gym, or scuba diving in Florida's springs. They're part of the 50 sport and recreation-focused student organizations in FSU's Sport Club Program. Most students know about basketball, baseball, soccer and volleyball, but the other 46 clubs rarely get the spotlight. Here are five more worth knowing.

On Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, the FSU lakefront fills with sailboats with two sailors on each boat. Club Sailing at FSU sails 420s, which have one sailor steering and another controlling the smaller sail in the front of the boat, the jib. The competitive nature of the sailing club demands more than what most expect.

"I don't think people understand the time commitment," FSU biological sciences major Erinne Fenton said in an interview with the FSView. "A lot of people misjudge sailing and think it's a chill hobby where you don't have to do too much, but in racing it's more competitive and you have to spend a lot of time and effort to be good."

There is a sailing club team, which consists of students who enjoyed one of the "learn-to-sail" events at the lakefront and would like to continue their sailing adventures. The competitive team, on the other hand, traveled weekly to regattas across Florida and South Carolina from September to October 2026.

"Sailing wrapped up their season at the Women's and Co-ed fall fleet racing championships," competitive sailing team captain Peter Foley said in an interview with the FSView. "Women's finished 7th overall and co-ed finished 9th with a standout 3rd place finish in A division."

Several FSU students spend their afternoons and weekends catching black bass or other game fish using a rod, reel, line, and lures. The Bass Fishing Club at FSU competes in the Bassmaster College Series and Major League Fishing Abu Garcia College Fishing circuits, rivaling schools across the country.

"Our goal is to build one of the premier collegiate bass fishing programs in the Southeast, and we want the FSU community to know that fishing is a real competitive sport here," Bass Fishing Club President Lucas Saraiva said in an interview with the FSView. "Beyond the college circuits, we host in-club tournaments, give back through lake cleanups, and bring anglers of every experience level together through social events and a shared love for the sport."

The club recognized Florida State alumnus Drew Cook, a professional angler and finished 3rd place in the Bassmaster Elite Series Angler of the Year standings.

He was also named the 2019 Bassmaster Rookie of the Year, earned a Century Belt in 2022, and has achieved multiple Bassmaster Classic appearances and top finishes.

Every Tuesday and Thursday evening, you can catch members of the Climbing Club at FSU at Alchemy Climbing, a rock gym in Tallahassee. They've climbed both in and out-of-state, in Tennessee, and in Alabama.

"Climbing Club at FSU is a great way for students to get out of their comfort zone, try new things, and connect with nature through camping and outdoor climbing trips," junior information, communication, and technology major Aidan Logvinov said in an interview with the FSView. "Whether you're new to the sport and trying it for the first time in the gym, or you're an experienced climber looking for a community, Climbing Club at FSU has something for everyone."

The climbing club plans three to four climbing trips every semester, and there also participate in competitions hosted by USA Climbing. In these competitions, climbers can compete in boulder, speed, or lead climbing. Lead or boulder climbing begins with a redpoint/qualifier format where climbers have a set window of two to three hours to complete multiple routes, followed by an on-sight final, while speed climbing is head-to-head or timed runs on a standard wall.

The FSU Jiu-Jitsu Club teaches Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, a martial art built on grappling and self-defense. Members train three times a week and often team up with other student groups, from Greek life to Reserve Officers' Training Corps.

The club's goal is to foster a welcoming and supportive community where students can challenge themselves, build confidence, and form meaningful friendships. In an interview with the FSView, Jiu Jitsu Club President Nico De La Cadena said he doesn't want anyone to feel intimidated by the idea of trying martial arts.

"Despite the intimidating reputation martial arts can sometimes have, some of the kindest, most humble, and most supportive people I've met have been through Jiu-Jitsu," President of the Jiu Jitsu club, Nico De La Cadena said in an interview with the FSView. "Ultimately, we want students to know that regardless of their experience or athletic background, there is a place for them in our club."

SCUBA at FSU is an official affiliate of the FSU Campus Recreation Sport Club Program, active in the local diving community for over 60 years. This club also isn't just for those that are ready immediately to get scuba certified. Those without certifications can snorkel, swim, or just join the club when they're at a diving site.

The club offers an open water diver course, which costs $350 for students and $400 for non-students and includes equipment, course packets, and state park dive fees. This club has had dives across Florida in rivers and springs like Troy Springs, Vortex Spring, Morrison Springs, Blue Grotto, Fanning Springs, and Rainbow River.

"Our club provides a space for FSU students who are either SCUBA certified or interested in getting certified to connect and dive with each other," social media coordinator for the SCUBA club, Jen Scheckowitz, said in an interview with the FSView. "The most common misconception about our club is that you have to hold a scuba certification to be a part of it."

Kayra Serpenguzel is a Senior Staff Writer for the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com.

This article originally appeared on FSU News: Five sports clubs at Florida State you should know about

#2741. Observations after Sixers survive Bucks' late surge, reach 14-3

Observations after Sixers survive Bucks' late surge, reach 14-3 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers survived the Bucks' late surge and reached 14-3 on the season Saturday afternoon with a 132-129 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Tyler Herro nearly sent the game to overtime with a buzzer-beating three-pointer, but replays showed that he released his shot late.

Herro had a massive performance for the 1-16 Bucks, posting a career-high 50 points on 15-for-23 shooting, 11 rebounds and seven assists.

Joel Embiid had 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the Sixers.

LeBron James (21 points), Tyrese Maxey (17 points) and Anfernee Simons (18) were among the seven Sixers to score in double figures.

The Sixers were down Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain), Dean Wade (left hamstring tightness/soreness), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear).

Next up for the Sixers is a Monday night meeting with the Trail Blazers. Here are observations on their victory over the Bucks:

Maxey returned to the Sixers' starting five after missing the team's comeback win Wednesday over the Magic with right foot soreness. He was joined by VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid.

James threw down a dunk on the day's first play. Embiid then dished to a cutting Edgecombe for a layup that put the Sixers up 4-0.

The Bucks quickly found a foothold in the game.

Embiid missed his first four shots, including two that were swatted by Myles Turner. Maxey began 1 for 5 from the floor. Herro canned a three-pointer to give Milwaukee a 15-8 lead.

The Sixers entered the game with a minus-13.2 net rating in first quarters, which ranked 28th in the NBA. They faced a 30-29 deficit after Saturday's first period.

Even with Maxey available again, Labaron Philon Jr. deservingly stayed in the Sixers' rotation following an excellent outing in Orlando.

He scored two points in six first-half minutes. The 20-year-old made a rookie mistake at the tail end of the first quarter, fouling Herro on a three-point attempt.

Dominick Barlow checked in for his first action of the season with 2:51 remaining in the first quarter. He'd been sidelined for the Sixers' first 16 games because of a lower back stress reaction.

Barlow scored his first points early in the second quarter when he tipped in a Maxey miss. He then teamed up with James in crowd-pleasing style, sprinting ahead of the pack on a fast break and flushing home the 22-time All-Star's long-distance lob.

The afternoon was not devoid of rust for Barlow. Shortly after that alley-oop, he grabbed an offensive rebound, dribbled out to the perimeter and fired an open three-pointer … which he air balled short.

To Barlow's credit, he took another three early in the fourth quarter and drained it. He logged 11 minutes and was quite productive, tallying 12 points on 5-for-6 shooting and four rebounds.

"It felt great," Barlow said of his three. "Got to shoot the ball with confidence. … I've obviously got to get a game feel; I've been missing that. But I worked too hard (in the offseason) to not shoot the ball when I'm open."

Kyle Kuzma hit a three late in the second quarter to build the Bucks' lead to 59-52. After Sixers head coach Nick Nurse's timeout, the team closed the first half on a 8-0 run featuring an Embiid dunk.

The Sixers went just 3 for 16 from long range in the first half, but their low-turnover ways helped mitigate those shooting struggles.

They committed a single turnover in the first half and finished with four giveaways. That's tied for their lowest ever on record in a single game. The Sixers have the NBA's lowest turnover percentage outside of garbage time, according to Cleaning the Glass.

"No matter who you're playing against, teams try to turn you over, they try to speed you up," James said. "Us taking care of the ball, that's a lot of the reason why we won this game."

The Sixers' shooters were bound to start sinking some open looks eventually. Simons, Caldwell-Pope and Edgecombe all made threes late in the third quarter and the team's lead grew as high as 13 points.

Thanks largely to Herro's individuals exploits, the Bucks stayed competitive. AJ Green buried a corner three to cut Milwaukee's deficit to 106-103 with 8:10 to go in the game.

James sought out his shot much more following the Sixers' timeout and did so with great success. He scored four buckets inside over the next four minutes, including a big slam that put the Sixers up 121-112.

It appeared the main questions left were whether Embiid could reach a triple-double and just how many points Herro would rack up.

However, the Bucks forced the Sixers to work down the stretch. Herro got to the 50-point milestone and trimmed the Sixers' lead to two points when he converted a layup with 19.2 seconds left.

The Sixers safely navigated to the final buzzer by the slimmest of margins. Embiid made four late free throws and everyone on the Sixers' sideline was relieved to see that Herro hadn't quite released his jumper in time.

"I try not to complain too much about any win in this league," Nurse said. "The message is we've got to finish a little better."

#2735. James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers

James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James likes to refer to the NBA season as a "marathon."

A few miles in, the Sixers lead the Eastern Conference pack.

With 17 regular-season contests down of 82, the team sits at 14-3, which is 2.5 games ahead of the second-seeded Celtics. The Sixers squeaked out their latest win, a 132-129 decision Saturday over the cellar-dwelling Bucks, but the bottom line is they've become accustomed to finding many routes to victory.

"We want to build habits," James said. "We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity. I know sometimes it doesn't happen that way, but we want to do it.

"We want to strive to be as great as we can offensively, defensively and on special teams. A win is a win, but there's ways to win and ways to try to continue to build habits over the course of a marathon."

All sorts of Sixers games have gone down to the wire and they've won every single one.

The team is an incredible 12-0 in clutch situations, defined as games with a point differential of five or under in the final five minutes. The Sixers rank third in the NBA in clutch offensive rating (140.3) and third in clutch net rating (plus-42.0).

"It's good to build that part of our game," James said. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they're going to be scrappy. They're going to play as hard as they can for 48 minutes. … We can learn from that."

James was the centerpiece of the Sixers' fourth-quarter offense Saturday. He scored 13 of his 21 points between the 7:46 and 3:13 mark of the fourth.

The four-time MVP got two buckets on no-nonsense drives and another on an after-timeout isolation hoop over rookie Brayden Burries. James also scored three times on a designed Horns action where he brought the ball up, used Tyrese Maxey's back screen at the elbow and caused serious problems for Milwaukee in the paint.

"We continue to add things to the half-court offense and also to the late-game package," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "That's something we added a few game ago. It's one of those things where, especially if we're in the bonus, we've got some big bodies that can cut down the lane and have feel for timing. It was working. Just keep going to it."

James has grown in comfort with Nurse's coaching style. He knows the Sixers expect him to be a de facto coach on the floor, too.

"I'm just trying to be there for the team in any capacity they want," he said. "Just trying to be an extension of his calls and his commands out there on the floor. Trying to make his life and his job a little bit easier as well.

"But it's been great, not only with him but the whole coaching staff. They've welcomed me with open arms and allowed me to kind of be the voice for the team every day, and take that responsibility."

After a tremendous first impression defensively and some subpar offensive nights, the Sixers' numbers have recently evened out.

The team is 12th in offensive rating outside of garbage time and 12th in defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. In essence, the Sixers have been a bit above average on both ends of the floor and downright brilliant in the closing minutes.

It's all added up to an early lead in a very long race.

"I think we've bought into the pass," James said. "We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels. … In order for us to be a super-complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious. And it's also key for our other guys, to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident. We've done that from Day 1 and I think it's gotten better and better. … And I think our defense has been really good for the majority of the season.

"(Today) it wasn't so great, but we've been very good defensively throughout the course of the season. … I don't want to say there's anything bad. There's so many things for us to do better for sure. There's games where we can defensive rebound a lot better and there's games where we can not turn the ball over (as much). And there's games where we can be a little more phsyical defensively at the point of attack like (today).

"I wouldn't say anything has been bad, though. That's a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement and we don't want to be great in November. That would be weird."

#2731. Has Rasul Douglas been Adam Peters’ best off season addition?

Following an extended time period on injured reserve for 2025 second-round pick Trey Amos, the Washington Commanders added Rasul Douglas late in free agency, signing the veteran just before the start of training camp in July. At the time, there were multiple questions surrounding the addition of a soon-to-be 31-year-old cornerback for a team that desperately needed playmakers in the secondary.

Douglas worked behind fellow cornerbacks Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson to start the season, and while he only played 38% of the team's total defensive snaps in Week 1, Rasul immediately made a mark with his physical play style.

Eventually, Douglas would take over a full-time role for the Commanders' defense in Week 4, logging 85% of the total defensive snaps and recording 5 tackles, 1 assist, 2 stops, 1 interception, and 1 pass defended versus the Colts. Post-game, Rasul proved his fit for Washington's competitive culture, stating the secondary's improved performance was not good enough, as the team didn't win the matchup. The following week, Douglas backed his words with his own play, finishing second on the team with 9 tackles and 1 assist while being graded with 4 receptions for 39 receiving yards allowed on 9 targets by Pro Football Reference.

Trey Amos returned to the lineup in Week 6, and while his return, along with the addition of safety Nick Cross, has been attributed to the improvement of the Commanders' secondary, Douglas' performance as a third cornerback cannot be overlooked. Since Week 6 in San Francisco, Washington's defense has given up just 18.5 points per game and the secondary has not allowed more than one passing touchdown in each of those contests. While that stretch did include games against the struggling Eagles and last week's road trip to New York, it also included games against the 49ers and Rams. Through Week 10, per @SFdata9ers, Douglas has a league-low 39.6 allowed passer rating while also leading the team in interceptions with 3, including a game-sealing grab at Metlife Stadium.

Identified in the off-season as a potential fit for Daronte Jones' defensive scheme, in addition to being a ball-hawk, Douglas has been a sure tackler, recording 29 total tackles (22 solo) on the season and 7 passes defended; just 2 behind full-time starter Amik Robertson. With Robertson's availability in question for Monday night's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals' elite passing offense, Douglas may be called on to prove his value yet again, but fans may take comfort in the fact the Commanders' cornerback ranks 9th on Pro Football Network's cornerback grading list headed into Week 11.

What is the best part of Rasul Douglas' performance thus far?

He was signed to a 1-year, $1.8 million agreement with only $580k of guaranteed money and up to $2 million available in incentives. Those numbers rank him 95th on Spotrac's average cornerback contract rankings, yet halfway through the season, Douglas is playing at a top ten level. That makes the free agent addition arguably the best of Adam Peters' off season acquisitions so far and a player the Washington Commanders should consider keeping around next season.

#2730. What’s the current relationship between Jayden Daniels and Joe Burrow?

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow have a lot in common. Both quarterbacks began their college careers at other schools before transferring to LSU, where they played their final two years.

After a solid first year in Baton Rouge, both exploded during their final season with the Tigers. Burrow led LSU to the 2019 national championship and won the Heisman Trophy. Daniels didn't win a national championship with the Tigers, but he did win the 2023 Heisman Trophy.

Burrow and Daniels are two of only three LSU players — and the only quarterbacks — to win the Heisman Trophy. Burrow went No. 1 overall to the Cincinnati Bengals in the 2020 NFL Draft, while Daniels became the No. 2 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft to the Commanders.

On Monday, they meet for the second time in their NFL careers. Back in Daniels' 2024 rookie season, the Commanders and Bengals met in Week 3. Washington, heavy underdogs, shocked the Bengals on the road, winning 38-33. Both quarterbacks were outstanding, but Daniels, in his third NFL start, outduelled Burrow. He completed 21 of 23 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns. He also rushed for one. His game-clinching touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin was one of the best passes of that entire season.

With so much in common, what's the extent of the relationship between the two former LSU stars?

"It's good. I mean, Joe is a guy that we built a kind of relationship over these years," Daniels said of Burrow. "Competitors always rooting for each other. So every time I see Joe, man, it's all love."

It's no surprise to see Daniels and Burrow having a solid relationship. However, that's all out the window on Monday night. Daniels looks to improve to 2-0 against Burrow and Cincinnati.

This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: What's the current relationship between Jayden Daniels and Joe Burrow?

#2728. The Colts, as expected, won't activate WR Alec Pierce from injured reserve

As the Colts fully embrace the making of business decisions over the pursuit of victories, this one is no surprise.

Via Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL, the Colts won’t activate receiver Alec Pierce from injured reserve. He’ll miss the rest of the season, with the goal of being fully and completely healthy for 2027.

The situation with Pierce becomes just another one of the tangible examples of the manner in which everything has gone sideways for the Colts over the past calendar year, starting with the November 2025 trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner. Despite knowing that Pierce had an ankle issue that would eventually require surgery, the Colts re-signed Pierce at the outset of free agency to a four-year deal with an annual average of $28.5 million.

While well below the top of the market at the position, it was a major investment in a player with a significant injury. Pierce had surgery in late March and played two games in September (catching five passes for 72 yards) before landing on injured reserve due to an aggravation of the condition.

Given the timing of the deal with Pierce (it was announced just as the March 9 negotiating window opened), it appears that the Colts put a number on the table aimed at keeping him from taking a comparable deal elsewhere. With the Colts promptly trading receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to the Steelers, and in light of the limited production they’ve gotten from Pierce this year, it’s very easy to conclude they should have let Pierce walk, keeping Pittman and moving on.

At this point, with the team at 3-8 and pivoting to quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr., there’s no reason to rush Pierce back. From the moment the Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, the Colts threw in the shoe on 2026. Everything that has happened since then serves only to highlight the fact that they no longer care about 2026 (to the delight of the Jets, who hold Indy’s first-round pick next year), and that they’re trying to best position themselves for 2027.

Keeping Pierce on IR is just another obvious aspect of that broader plan. And it bolsters the possibility that owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon will decide to give coach Shane Steichen another year.

After a hard-fought Week 7 game at Minnesota saw a potential 3-4 record slip to 2-5, the “we’ll get ‘em next year” plan was fully activated. While Steichen can be held accountable for the first seven games, it’s hard to pin much blame on him for the final ten.

#2726. Seahawks will finish 5-2 in final 7 games after bye week

How well will the Seattle Seahawks finish the 2026 NFL season over the course of their final seven games coming out of their bye week in Week 11?

The Seahawks will go 5-2 over the course of their final seven games, leaning on an improved rushing attack and timely home victories to strengthen their postseason positioning.

Following the Seahawks' bye, the team will visit San Francisco in Week 12 and host Dallas in Week 13, as well as the Giants in Week 14, before visiting Philadelphia in Week 15, hosting the Rams in Week 16, and closing out the year with two road matchups against Carolina in Week 17 and the Rams in Week 18.

The forecast begins with a loss against San Francisco. Arguably the league's best team, the 49ers possess greater momentum, and have more offensive cohesion as well as a comparable amount of potency on defense to challenge Seattle throughout the game. The Seahawks will have extra preparation time coming off their bye, but the time off serves as a double-edged sword, which will contribute to the loss.

Seattle will rebound with victories over Dallas, the Giants, Philadelphia and the Rams. The Cowboys present a tough hurdle in that sequence, with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens figuring to challenge the defense greatly. However, home-field advantage, coupled with a stout Seattle secondary will be the deciding factor of the Week 16 matchup against Los Angeles. Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price will have several additional weeks to establish a productive groove, giving Seattle the rushing balance necessary to sustain drives, manage possession and protect a narrow lead.

The Rams will also be a tough challenge in Week 16, but with a projected three-game winning streak going for the Seahawks entering the matchup, the team will hand Los Angeles a loss. Seattle is also projected to defeat Carolina in Week 17, extending its winning streak to five. A road loss against the Rams in Week 18 will end that surge, but Seattle will still complete a strong closing stretch of the year and cement itself in the postseason picture.

That stretch will lift Seattle from 6-4 to an 11-6 finish.

This article originally appeared on Seahawks Wire: Seahawks will finish 5-2 in final 7 games after bye week

#2724. Steelers try for first win in Philadelphia since LBJ was president

That’s the last time the Pittsburgh Steelers won a regular-season game in Philadelphia.

LBJ was president. Bonanza was the top show on TV. Yesterday was the No. 1 song.

The Steelers entered that game 0-5. The Eagles were 2-3. Pittsburgh’s quarterback was Bill Nelsen. Philly’s was Jack Concannon.

The 20-14 final score was fueled by a pair of defensive scores. Willie Daniel returned a fumble 17 yards for a touchdown. Jim Bradshaw had an 82-yard interception return for another six. (He had three interceptions in the game.)

The Eagles otherwise dominated. They gained 388 yards. The Steelers gained 132. Pittsburgh fumbled five times, but recovered four of them. Running back Dick Hoak, who passed away recently, led Pittsburgh with 46 yards from scrimmage.

Since that day, the Eagles are 11-0 at home against the Steelers. Today, in a game that was flexed out of the 4:25 p.m. ET window because the Eagles are in a soft-tank free fall, the Steelers are 6-3 and the Eagles are 2-7.

For the Steelers, a loss today could see 6-3 become 6-7 quickly; their next three games are against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars.

So beyond ending a 61-year streak of futility in Philly, the Steelers need to win this one today. Even if they do, those next three games could alter the trajectory of the season and throw the Steelers into a scramble for a playoff berth in a stretch run that includes the Ravens, Panthers, Titans, and Ravens.

#2723. NFL wife opens up on chaotic 24 hours after Chiefs cut returner ‘out of the blue’

While life in the NFL may seem glamorous, one NFL WAG is giving fans a peek at the chaos it can also entail in a post on social media.

Maureen Remigio, a former Philippine track and field star and the wife of NFL wide receiver and return specialist Nikko Remigio, shared the blow-by-blow of what it was like to learn that her husband had been cut by the Chiefs earlier this month.

Nikko Remigio had been Kansas City's starting punt returner for three years before the decision was made to cut him in order to make room for the newly acquired Josh Downs, whom the Chiefs picked up in a trade with the Colts on Nov. 10.

Maureen began spilling the tea — while drinking Chinese herbal tea in her video — about how Nikko had first became aware of the move when he received a text "out of the blue" from the Chiefs.

"We just got a text that he needs to come in, bring his iPad and that's it," she explained in her social media post. "Really just want to make you guys understand how quick everything happens."

With Nikko on waivers, he was free to be picked up by any NFL team that wanted to put a claim in on him, and Maureen explained the torture that goes into the 24-hour period when a player could be picked up by another team.

Houston Texans wide receiver Nikko Remigio returns a kick against Cleveland Browns wide receiver Malachi Corley on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Cleveland. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

"Within those 24 hours, you don't know where you're going," she said. "You don't know who's going to get you, if you're going to get claimed or not, and what your options are.

"So you can just imagine the waiting game, the sitting around, the walking around the house, the uncertainty that just happened in a snap of a finger. "Almost close to the 24th hour was when we found out that the Texans claimed Nikko."

Maureen Remigio at a Chiefs game mauemily/Instagram

But the chaos wasn't over just yet for the Remigios.

The Texans booked Nikko's flight out of Kansas City for a little more than two hours after he found out he was headed to Houston, meaning a mad scramble to get things together and get to the airport.

Maureen described just throwing clothes into his suitcase and rushing him to the airport, and "just like that, he's in Houston."

Nikko made his debut for the Texans in their loss to the Browns in Week 10, averaging 28.5 yards on kickoff returns and 14.5 yards on punt returns.

But Maureen's post was a glimpse into the side of a "very cold business sometimes."

"This is just the side of professional football that not a lot of people understand," she explained. "Like you can have a job yesterday and the next day you might not have a job. Not all athletes' contracts are guaranteed and Nikko, being an undrafted free agent, he has always had to fight for his spot on the roster, and now I'm just excited to be with him."

#2721. The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats!

The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats! originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

This 76ers team is a heck of a lot of fun to watch and fun basketball means fun stats!

At 13-3, the 76ers are exactly a month into the 5th-best start in franchise history and best since they were 14-2 in 2000-01. Which turned out to be a pretty good year. They were 15-1 in 1949-50 and 1966-67 and 14-2 in 1981-82.

To help everybody get through this interminable two-day gap between 76ers games, here's our first 2026-27 installment of Roob's 76ers Stats, with a tip of the hat to Stathead.

→ The 76ers have been out-rebounded by 34 through 16 games (719-685) and their 13-3 record matches the best in NBA history by a team that's been out-rebounded after 16 games. Three other teams have been 13-3 despite getting out-rebounded, most recently the 2013-14 Miami Heat. The others are the 1979-80 Bucks and 2012-2013 Spurs. The 76ers are an NBA-best 6-3 this year when they've been out-rebounded (which means they're 7-0 when they have a rebounding edge).

→ In the win over Orlando Thursday, V.J. Edgecombe had 24 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, and Joel Embiid had 26 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two steals. It was the first time two 76ers had at least 24 points, six rebounds and assists and two steals in a game in 53 years. In a win over the Celtics at the Spectrum in 1973, Fred Carter had 31 points, six rebounds, six assists and seven steals and George McGinniss had 28 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists and three steals.

→ Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a career 37 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 44 percent so far. Anfernee Simons, a career 38 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 41 percent. Jabari Walker, a career 33 percent 3-point shooter, is at 42 percent. Dean Wade, a career 37 percent shooter, is at 41 percent. Jaylen Brown, a career 36 percent shooter from range, is at 39 percent. The 76ers are shooting just 36 percent as a team from the stripe because James and Embiid have been so bad, but everybody else is off to career-best starts from 3-point range.

→ The 76ers are 7-1 on the road, equalling their best road record ever after eight games. They were also 7-1 in 1980-81, 1981-82 and 1982-83. The 1981 team had the best road start in franchise history, going 12-1 before losing its second road game.

→ With 15.7 points, 6.8 assists and 6.8 rebounds per game, LeBron James is only the fifth 76er ever to average at least 15 ½ points and 6 ½ assists and rebounds through 16 games. The others are some familiar names: Wilt Chamberlain in 1967, Charles Barkley in 1987, Ben Simmons in 2018 and James Harden in 2023.

→ The 76ers already have more wins this year after trailing by 10 points through the first quarter than all but two full seasons since 1950. They had four in 1985-86 and again in 2022-23. The Hawks also have three wins this year when trailing by double digits after the first quarter, but they're 3-4 and the 76ers are 3-2. So they actually have a winning record when they're down by double digits going into the second quarter.

→ With Jaylen Brown (22.6, 6.6), Joel Embiid (20.0, 8.3), LeBron James (15.7, 6.8) and V.J. Edgecombe (13.6, 6.5), the 76ers are the only NBA team with four players averaging 6 ½ rebounds and 13 points. The last time they had four players in a season who averaged 13 points and 6 ½ rebounds was 1961-62 when they were the Syracuse Nationals, with Dave Gambee (16.7, 7.9), Hal Greer (22.8, 7.4), Red Kerr (16.3, 14.7), Dolph Schayes (14.7, 7.8) and Lee Shaffer (16.9, 6.8).

→ Edgecombe's 6.5 rebounds per game are 2nd-most among shooting guards behind only the Grizzlies' Cedric Coward, who is at 8.5. Edgecombe's 6.5 is also 2nd-highest ever by a 76ers shooting guard behind only Greer's 7.4 during that 1961-62 season. Edgecombe averaged 5.6 rebounds as a rookie and his 5.8 career average is highest by a shooting guard who spent more than one year with the 76ers. Greer is second at 5.3. Among all NBA players who've played at least 90 games, Edgecombe's 5.8 average is 11th-highest all-time among shooting guards (although Stathead includes some swing guard-forwards in their data).

→ Joel Embiid's 14.6 shooting percentage from 3 is worst in NBA history after 16 games (minimum 40 attempts). Embiid is 6-for-41 from the stripe this year. The previous 3-point shooting low 16 games into a season belonged to Cedric Ceballos of the Lakers in 1995-96 and the 76ers' Evan Turner in 2013-14. Both were 6-for-43 for 16.3 percent.

→ LeBron James is at 22.2 percent from 3 on 10-for-45. The Sixers are the first NBA team in 12 years with two players under 23 percent after 16 games with a minimum of 40 attempts. In 2014 Tony Wroten was 10-for-50 (10 percent) and Turner was 6-for-43 (16.3 percent).

"It obviously sucks to lose, but you've got to give credit to Kansas [City]. They were very dominant. They were very together and they finished their chances."

#2719. Report: Daniel Jones is likely to wait to sign with the "right team at the right time"

Any team can claim the contract of quarterback Daniel Jones on waivers before the Monday deadline. Given the $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027, which becomes a full guarantee if he suffers an injury that prevents him from passing a physical by March, it’s unlikely that any will.

And so he’ll become a free agent, like he did after he was benched (for financial reasons) and then cut by the Giants two years ago today.

Via ESPNFL, Jones is “unlikely” to sign with another team immediately. His preference, per the report, will be to “wait for the right opportunity with the right team at the right time.”

There’s a cake-and-eat-it option not mentioned by the new report. Jones can sign with a practice squad, giving him the flexibility to jump to another team’s active roster in the event the planets align for Jones to step in and play for a contender in relevant late-season games.

That’s what he did in 2024, joining the Minnesota practice squad while keeping the ability to jump to a 53-man roster elsewhere.

Why wouldn’t he do that again? It would keep him working within the confines of an NFL team, which could result in reports that he’s looking much better there than he did during his 2026 season in Indianapolis, which had him dead last among all qualifying quarterbacks with a passer rating of 65.4.

Whether he chooses to do that or not, it becomes an obvious (if not likely) option for Jones. Especially since he did the exact same thing the last time he found himself benched and then released.

#2717. Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory

Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stretched their winning streak to four games and snagged a strong road win Wednesday night over the Magic.

They earned a 121-116 victory in Orlando to improve to 13-3 on the season. The Magic dropped to 6-8.

Joel Embiid had 26 points, seven assists, six rebounds, three blocks and two steals.

VJ Edgecombe posted a season-high 24 points, eight boards and six assists.

LeBron James scored 22 points and Anfernee Simons added 18.

Magic star Franz Wagner had 27 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds.

The Sixers had a long injury list in Orlando. Tyrese Maxey (right foot soreness), Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain) and Dean Wade (left hamstring soreness/tightness) were among their players out. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters in Orlando that Brown will be re-evaluated when the team returns to Philadelphia.

Orlando was without star forward Paolo Banchero (right high ankle sprain).

The Sixers will start a three-game homestand when they face the Bucks on Saturday afternoon. Here are observations on their win over the Magic:

The Sixers' undermanned starting lineup was Edgecombe, Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid.

After scoring 37 points in the Sixers' win over the Nets, Embiid had a subpar start. He began 1 for 6 from the floor and committed a turnover that led to an Anthony Black dunk.

The Sixers' lineup looked exactly like a unit that hadn't built any chemistry yet. The team was not sharp early on either end of the floor.

Desmond Bane drained a long three-pointer to give Orlando a 27-12 advantage. Orlando made 11 of its first 14 field goals and led by as many as 17 points in the first quarter.

Labaron Philon Jr. and Justin Edwards joined the Sixers' rotation. So did two-way contract players Tacko Fall and Caleb Love.

Philon impressed in the first quarter, converting two floaters and a corner three. The rookie passed his previous NBA scoring high of five points and finished the night with 10 on 4-for-5 shooting.

Fall played 10 minutes and posted two points, three rebounds and three blocks. He slammed in a dunk and rejected two shots early in the second quarter. Credit to Fall for giving the Sixers a good backup center performance and doing his job as a rim-protecting ultra-big man.

Love entered in the second quarter and was ready to fire, hitting a catch-and-shoot three-pointer on his first touch.

The Sixers' zone defense also helped them eat into the Magic's lead. The zone seemed to disrupt Orlando's offensive rhythm and it was active enough to prevent the Magic from consistently creating high-quality looks.

Edgecombe's buzzer-beating mid-range jumper cut the Sixers' deficit to 69-64 after two quarters.

The Sixers pulled within a single point on multiple occasions in the third quarter, including on a Philon three late in the period. They trailed by five points after the third.

Fall continued to play well early in the fourth quarter. He deterred the Magic's drivers from getting all the way to the rim as the very large back line of the Sixers' zone defense and made eye-catching hustle plays on both sides of the ball.

The Sixers outscored Orlando by seven points on the night with Fall on the court. Soon after Embiid subbed back in, he evened the game at 104-all with two free throws. Jabari Walker swished a three to finally push the Sixers in front.

The Magic regained a late lead with a Jalen Suggs three. James then drove and kicked the ball out to Edgecombe, who nailed one of his customary clutch jumpers to put the Sixers back on top.

No matter the night-to-night personnel, the Sixers have been fantastic at the tail end of close games. They're now 11-0 in clutch situations, which the NBA defines as games within a five-point differential in the final five minutes.

#2713. 3 thoughts ahead of the Mavericks’ back-to-back bonanza at the Utah Jazz

It may feel like the season just started, but the Dallas Mavericks (9-7) are already in the middle of the team's fourth back-to-back set as they turn the team charter toward the great Salt Lake, with a quick turnaround before facing the Utah Jazz (3-14) at the Delta Center. The Mavericks beat the Los Angeles Clippers (4-11) at home on Saturday, 110-100.

Dallas salvaged a clunker on Saturday, and if there is one thing the Jazz are accustomed to this year, it's clunkers.

Let's take a swim in the salty waters out west and get a look at what lies ahead for the Mavs in Utah.

The back end of a back-to-back set for the Mavericks is the front end of one for Utah in this one. The Jazz are coming off of Friday's 111-101 home loss to the Phoenix Suns. Rookie guard Darryn Peterson was gaining some steam earlier in November with five straight games of 21 or more points before a three-game lull preceded his 20-point night in the loss to the Suns. Still, he's shooting just 36.3% from the field and just 26.1% from 3-point range in his last four.

While Peterson is averaging 16.7 points per game through the first 17 games of his NBA career, Keyonte George leads the team at 21.1 points and 7.1 assists per game, while key contributors Lauri Markkanen (hand), Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee), and noted Mavs killer Jusuf Nurkic (foot) will all miss Sunday's game with injuries. As a result, the Jazz come into the game against Dallas with an offensive rating of just 106.9, next to last in the league, ahead of only the Charlotte Hornets (103.1). They're 25th in the NBA in net rating, at -7.7.

The Mavs had some trouble putting the struggling Clippers away in the front end of their back-to-back set on Saturday, but Sunday's game in Utah presents another opportunity to hone that edge to their game that has been hit-and-miss since the team's 7-4 start to the year.

Keep an eye on who is available for the Mavericks ahead of Sunday's game in Utah. Kyrie Irving, who scored 25 points on 8-of-24 shooting in 35 minutes in Saturday's win over the Clippers, has played in both legs of one of the three previous back-to-back sets so far this season. We're just guessing, but the established trend and the opponent offer the Mavs another opportunity to do the "injury management" dance.

The Mavs were also without PJ Washington (illness) on Saturday, and while the hope would be that one game off would be enough to get Washington right, we won't know for sure until about noon on Sunday for sure on their status. If those two are unable to go, the viewing experience could end up anywhere from "meh" to downright brutal.

Lost in the slog of Saturday's squeaker over the Clippers was a rare good shooting night from Max Christie. On a night when Cooper Flagg's shot diet (6-of-16 from the field) was downright unhealthy and the rest of the offense sputtered around him, the Mavericks needed all 13 of Christie's points in his 24 minutes on the floor after he had worked his way into the Dusty May Phantom Zone after a slow start to the year.

Both Christie and Walter Clayton Jr. (16 points, 5-of-8 shooting, 2-of-3 from 3-point range) were positives off the bench for the Mavericks, and they will both likely be called upon to do it again on Sunday, especially if Irving is inactive.

The Mavericks and the Jazz tip off at 6 p.m. on Sunday at the Delta Center. The game will be televised locally on KFAA Channel 29, or you can catch the stream on MavsTV or NBA League Pass where available. The radio call can be heard on KRLD 105.3 The Fan.

#2712. Manchester City Women 1-3 Tottenham Women: Spurs secure HUGE win over defending champs

Tottenham Women have not had much luck against the best teams in the WSL. They've already fallen heavily to both London City and Chelsea this season, and few expected them to do much away at Manchester City, the defending league champions and league leaders heading into today's match.

But football can surprise you, sometimes in the best of ways. Tottenham went behind early after a cheap giveaway in their half and a quick-hit goal from WSL scoring leader Bunny Shaw, but Spurs kept their composure, outplayed City thoroughly, and put three in the net to defeat City 1-3. Tottenham's goals came from Tinka Tandberg, Matilda Vinberg, and substitute Jess Naz.

It's a season-defining win for Tottenham who have historically struggled against the top WSL clubs, and the result put Spurs, at least for now, fourth in the WSL table.

There was a shakeup before kickoff as midfielder (and Best Player in World WOSO) Olivia Holdt fell ill in the warmup and was scratched from the match. She was replaced in the lineup by Matilda Vinberg, otherwise it was the same starting XI as Tottenham's past two matches.

Bunny Shaw is ridiculous and amazing and I find it more or less impossible to dislike her, but stopping her was Tottenham's Plan A, B, and C. And they did! She had basically one shot, and she scored from it early on.

Spurs were committed to playing out of the back, at least early. No Route One football here, Martin Ho has an almost Postecoglou-like commitment to patient buildup and the high press.

And, like with under Ange, that's a double-edged sword. In this case, Drew Spence was dispossessed in the tenth minute inside her own half, City immediately fed Bunny who was wide open, and she scored past Kop to put City up 1-0. Live by playing out, die by playing out.

I'm just going to make this a Toko Koga appreciation comment. She's so good, incredible vision and passing from the back line, and a solid defender. And she's only 20! Spurs will face a tough task keeping ahold of her.

Apart from the early goal, Spurs outplayed. They were solid in possession, tested Yamashita a number of times including the equalizer, and looked good. Just shows you how one defensive slip can make a huge difference in a match.

I'm absolutely baffled how the penalty by Wamsa on Hanson wasn't called. It wasn't "shoulder-to-shoulder," Wamsa quite literally two-arm shoved Hanson to the ground and didn't make a play on the ball. I'm struggling to think of a more stonewall penalty not called this season and can't think of one. Insane.

Tinka Tandberg has struggled so far this season and was very quiet for most of the first half, but she one-timed a cross into the box from Hanson to level the score. Fantastic goal, and another incredible deep pass to Hanson from Toko Koga.

Tottenham's second goal came from another fantastic deep line-splitting pass, this time from Drew Spence to find Matilda Vinberg in the box. She got a half step on her defender with the ball and slotted past Yamashita to put Spurs ahead. Amazing!

ABSOLUTELY THRILLED for Jess Naz, who is fresh back from her second ACL injury and slots home Tottenham's third, her first goal since her return!

Look, Tottenham certainly have priors in big matches, especially in the league against the best teams — witness the heavy losses to London City and Chelsea already this season — but this is a MASSIVE win and a real statement of intent from Spurs.

Tottenham got big matches from both Victoria Pelova and Kirsty Hanson, who were menacing in City's box. Tottenham might have scored more thanks to their interplay in City's area.

It's, without hyperbole, the biggest win in club history. We talk about the North London Derby win, but in that one while Spurs defended heroically, they were under the cosh the entire match. In this match, Spurs went to the defending champions' home ground and played them off the park. Fantastic, outstanding, scintillating win.

Check out these final stats. Pretty, pretty good.

#2711. Colts reportedly shutting down WR Alec Pierce for remainder of 2026 season

The Indianapolis Colts are reportedly shutting down wide receiver Alec Pierce for the remainder of the 2026 season, prioritizing his long-term health as the organization prepares for another rebuilding period, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport.

Pierce has been sidelined since aggravating a left heel injury during Indianapolis' Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, the same heel he underwent surgery on during the offseason. The 26-year-old receiver missed nearly all of training camp before returning to practice in late August, only to suffer another setback shortly after the regular season began. He has been on injured reserve since September, with head coach Shane Steichen repeatedly declining to provide a definitive timetable for his return.

According to Rapoport, Pierce has been working extensively throughout his rehabilitation and had been pushing to return for the final few games of the season. However, the Colts are reportedly unwilling to risk another setback, instead focusing on having him fully healthy for the beginning of the 2027 campaign. While Pierce had hoped to return before the end of the year, the organization's decision effectively brings his disappointing 2026 season to an end after just two appearances.

The news comes during what has become an increasingly difficult season for Indianapolis, which has fallen to 3-8 following Thursday's loss to the Houston Texans. With the Colts already having traded several established veterans, including wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, the organization has little incentive to rush one of its most important offensive players back onto the field during a season that is unlikely to produce a playoff appearance.

Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million extension during the offseason following a breakout 2025 campaign in which he recorded 47 receptions for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns, leading the NFL in yards per reception for the second consecutive season. Expectations were understandably high entering 2026, with Pierce expected to become one of the central pieces of Indianapolis' offense. Instead, he finishes the season with just five receptions for 72 yards, a frustrating outcome for a player who had established himself as one of the league's most dangerous vertical threats.

His absence also leaves the Colts with an extremely inexperienced receiving corps over the remainder of the season. Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and rookie Deion Burks are among the remaining options, placing additional pressure on the younger players to contribute as Indianapolis evaluates its roster for the future. With Anthony Richardson now back under center following the release of Daniel Jones, having Pierce available would have provided a much-needed downfield threat, although protecting his long-term health is clearly the more important consideration.

From Indianapolis' perspective, the decision makes plenty of sense. Pierce is under contract through 2029 and remains one of the few established offensive players who could realistically contribute to the franchise's next competitive team. With significant changes expected during the offseason and a new general manager set to take over, ensuring Pierce returns fully healthy should be a much greater priority than attempting to squeeze a few additional games out of him during an increasingly disappointing season.

After an injury-plagued year that never truly got started, the Colts will now hope that a full offseason of recovery allows Pierce to return to the level that earned him one of the NFL's largest wide receiver contracts.

The NHL is not what it is today without Ovechkin and Crosby, and they entered the league together in 2005. They have faced off 100 times in the NHL, including 25 games in the playoffs. In those 100, they have combined for 231 points. A total of 90 games saw either find the score sheet and 49 had both record a point in the same game.

They have met in four postseason series, each in the second round. Crosby and the Penguins won the first three series and won the Cup each time. The Capitals won in 2018 and won their first and still only Stanley Cup. They have played 75 regular-season games in the series. Crosby leads 43-28-4 and has 35 goals and 62 assists in those. Ovechkin has 38 goals and 33 helpers.

The 39-year-old Crosby is in the final year of his contract but has said he has no plans to retire. He and Ovechkin have joined Howe, Alex Delvecchio, Stan Mikita and Steve Yzerman as the only players in NHL history to play 22 seasons with one franchise.

"Over the years, obviously, I've developed a friendship with him and have a ton of respect for him," Crosby said to the media Monday with the Ovechkin news. "It's tough, you come into the league at 18 years old, and before we even met, we were built up against each other."

It should be Logan Thompson in net for Washington, and he was excellent in his season debut in allowing two goals in a win at defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina last Friday. Last season at home, he was 19-9-5 with a 2.18 GAA and three shutouts. Thompson made two starts vs. Pittsburgh overall last campaign and won both with a 1.50 GAA.

The Penguins and Capitals have three meetings left, including Washington's home finale on April 4. That should be quite the Sunday night if both Crosby and Ovechkin are healthy then. Tickets on the secondary market are north of $800 to get in.

#2709. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2704. Wembanyama hits 50 points in dominant Spurs win

San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama hit 50 points in a historic performance as his side beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91.

The 22-year-old, who is 7ft 4ins tall, became the first player with 50 points, five blocks and five three-pointers in a match since the NBA added threes in 1979–80.

The France international, who was defensive player of the year for 2026, said he put on a show for a celebrity-packed crowd which included actress and long-time Spurs fan Selena Gomez.

"I just want to keep stacking them [records] up. I don't plan on doing those. They just come and we play the right way as a team.

"So, I just want to stack them up. Hopefully there's many more coming."

The Spurs have made a fine start to the season, winning 14 of their 17 games so far to top the Western Conference Southwest.

They won the division last season before losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals.

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson added. "It's a cliche to say, 'Why doesn't he do it every game?'

"But it's so interesting when people play like that, especially with his talent."

Wembanyama's haul - the third of his career - came after James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games on Saturday.

Wilt Chamberlain holds the record with an incredible 118 50-point games.

"It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat-padding," Wembanyama said.

"So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have."

Wembanyama was later asked whether there was an ethical right or wrong way to score 50 points. Some NBA players have been accused of chasing individual statistics for financial gain instead of concentrating on their team's results.

"Maybe, I think that's a question for you. The greats, they don't think about that," Wembanyama replied.

"I don't think LeBron [James], Shai [Gilgeous-Alexander], [Nikola] Jokic, [Luka] Doncic, I don't think they think about that. I have them as examples, so I'm trying to not think about it either."

#2703. SEC championship race comes down to Alabama, Texas, Tennessee. Here’s the catch

Finally, after many weeks of prognosticating, the SEC has unveiled a clear path to its conference championship game.

Following Week 12 of the college football season, the path has been made clear for each of Alabama, Texas and Tennessee football to make it to Atlanta and compete for one final conference title. The Crimson Tide, Longhorns and Volunteers already know they will play top-ranked Georgia, which clinched a spot in Atlanta with a 34-6 drubbing of South Carolina in Week 12.

SEC football live standings, results: Georgia clinches title game. Who will join?

That said, some paths to the SEC Championship are more direct than others. And none of Alabama, Texas or Tennessee is in full control of their destiny.

Here's how the Crimson Tide, Longhorns and Volunteers can make it to Atlanta to face off against Kirby Smart's Bulldogs:

Alabama win AND Tennessee loss AND Texas loss OR

Alabama win AND Tennessee win AND Texas win AND LSU win AND Mississippi State win

Kalen DeBoer and the Crimson Tide have two paths to the SEC title game. The simplest way for Alabama to make it is to beat Auburn and hope for losses by Tennessee and Texas, which would give the Crimson Tide a 7-2 record in SEC play, compared to the Longhorns and Vols' 6-3 marks.

However, there is a case in which all three teams win in Week 13 and Alabama still makes it. In the event of a three-way tie for second place, Alabama can still make it if LSU and Mississippi State also beat Arkansas and Mississippi, respectively.

In that scenario, the SEC would default to conference opponent win percentage, which would give Alabama (45.68%) the edge over Texas (44.44%) and Tennessee (43.21%). Curiously, this scenario only plays out in Alabama's favor if Tennessee and Texas also win in Week 13: A single deviation would result in either Texas or Tennessee making it over Alabama in a two-way tie.

Both Texas-Texas A&M and Ole Miss-Mississippi State play on Friday, Nov. 27, meaning Alabama fans will wake up on Nov. 28 knowing whether Atlanta's still on the table.

TOPPMEYER: Tennessee mugged LSU, Lane Kiffin. CFP committee will hate Vols anyway

Tennessee has the simplest path to SEC supremacy. It needs only to beat Vanderbilt and hope Texas A&M stuns Texas on Nov. 27, the day before the Vols play Vanderbilt. Should that happen, Josh Heupel and Co. will go to Atlanta.

Alabama has no bearing on whether Tennessee makes the SEC title game, as the Vols have a head-to-head win over DeBoer's squad. The only thing that matters is whether Tennessee can finish with a better conference record than Texas, who similarly has a head-to-head victory to rely on over the Vols.

REQUIRED READING: LSU hired Lane Kiffin to win big. He already has a worse season than any Brian Kelly had

Texas win AND Alabama win AND Tennessee win AND Mississippi State loss OR LSU loss

Like Alabama, Texas has multiple paths to the SEC. Two are simple: a loss by Alabama or a loss by Tennessee, which would move SEC tiebreakers into a two-way tie scenario, as opposed to a three-way tie. If Alabama were to lose, Texas would advance with a head-to-head victory to claim over Tennessee. If the Vols fell, Texas would advance based on a better conference win percentage over Alabama (4-0 vs. 3-1).

In the event Texas, Alabama and Tennessee all win in Week 13, forcing a three-way tiebreak scenario, the Longhorns can still make it if either Mississippi State or LSU loses. That would give the Longhorns, Crimson Tide and Vols a common win percentage among conference opponents (44.44%) but would lift Texas over Tennessee by way of head-to-head tiebreaker and over Alabama by way of record among common opponents.

#2701. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

Since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

For those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

David Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

Max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:

Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?"

I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

#2699. MLB rumors: Phillies OF on the trading block, Blue Jays eye ex-Yankee, plus Mets, Mariners, Braves, Rays, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

Phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

The Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

The Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a big bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

Marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

Happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

Yesterday's big news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

Bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

May, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He showed flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that says a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

Jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

Much has been said and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

As we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

DeLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

Fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

"We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to."

The Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

#2697. Open Thread: Spurs air “The Blueprint” honoring Harrison Barnes leadership and dedication

I was fortunate enough to attend the Emirates Cup game between the San Antonio Spurs and the Golden State Warriors. Not only was thirty-seven point drubbing a sight to behold, the energy in the arena was palpable. But there is something to watching the games from the comfort of my own couch. One of those is the commentary, another is the replays, and finally, there are the features.

When I finally rewatched the game on DAZN, I enjoyed this video presentation in the first act of the halftime break:

"The Blueprint" is a three-minute tribute honoring the Spurs veteran Harrison Barnes. Barnes originally came to San Antonio in a three-team trade involving the Spurs, Sacramento Kings, and Chicago Bulls. The trade sent DeMar DeRozan to Sacramento and included RaiQuan Gray, Chris Duarte, and led to Charles Bassey being waived.

Since arriving in San Antonio, Barnes has taken on a leadership role and offered a solid veteran presence to the fledgling Spurs team. He is a 2015 NBA Champion through his time with the Golden State Warriors. On the court, he's known for his consistent 3-point shooting and high basketball IQ. In the locker room, he exhibits an example of maturity and patience that lifted the team's spirits as they put the pieces together.
